title: Generic finite presentation of a finite module
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative integral domain, $B$ a commutative finite type $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], and $M$ a $B$-module generated by finitely many elements. There exists $0\ne a\in R$ such that $M_a$ is finitely presented over $B_a=B[1/a]$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. Here $M_a$ is the module of fractions $m/a^n$, with $m/a^n=m^{\prime}/a^k$ exactly when some power of $a$ annihilates $a^k m-a^n m^{\prime}$; finitely presented means that for some finite integers $u,v\ge0$ there is an exact sequence $B_a^u\to B_a^v\to M_a\to0$. No Noetherian or finite-presentation hypothesis on $B$ or $M$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 051T, algebra-lemma-generic-flatness, conclusion (b) for the module

proof.text: Choose a surjective $R$-algebra map $P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\to B$ from [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. A finite set $m_1,\ldots,m_t$ generating $M$ over $B$ also generates it over $P$: lift each coefficient in a $B$-linear expression to $P$. Thus $q:P^t\to M$, $(c_i)\mapsto\sum c_im_i$, is surjective. Put $N=\ker q$.

source.place: Tag 051T, algebra-lemma-generic-flatness, proof: polynomial case followed by general case

proof.text:
Let $K=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$, the field of fractions $r/s$ with $s
e0$, and define $V_K$ for each $R$-module $V$ as fractions $v/s$, where $v/s=w/u$ iff some $h
e0$ kills $uv-sw$. The map $P_K	o K[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ sends a polynomial divided by $s$ to the polynomial with coefficients divided by $s$; a common denominator for finitely many coefficients gives its inverse. The kernel of $q_K:P_K^t	o M_K$ is exactly the image of $N_K$: if $q(v)/s=0$, some $h
e0$ kills $q(v)$, so $hv\in N$ and $v/s=(hv)/(hs)$. Surjectivity follows by lifting the numerator of a fraction.

source.place: Tag 051T, algebra-lemma-generic-flatness, proof: polynomial case followed by general case

proof.text: A field is Noetherian because its only ideals are $(0)$ and $(1)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], $P_K=K[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ is Noetherian. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite] to the submodule $N_K\subseteq P_K^t$. Choose finite generators $z_i\in N_K$, write each $z_i=n_i/s_i$ with $n_i\in N$ and $0\ne s_i\in R$, and note that the $n_i/1$ also generate $N_K$, because $s_i$ is a unit in $K$.

source.place: Tag 051T, algebra-lemma-generic-flatness, proof: polynomial case followed by general case

proof.text: Put $H=\sum_iPn_i\subseteq N$ and $L=P^t/H$. This is finitely presented, with relation columns $n_i$, and the induced map $L\to M$ is surjective. For each $v\in N$, expressing $v/1$ in terms of the $n_i/1$ and taking a common nonzero denominator $s$ gives $sv/1=\sum_i c_i n_i/1$ with $c_i\in P$. Equality of fractions supplies $h\ne0$ with $h(sv-\sum_i c_i n_i)=0$, so $hs\,v\in H$. Hence every element of $\ker(L\to M)=N/H$ is killed by some nonzero element of $R$.

source.place: Tag 051T, algebra-lemma-generic-flatness, proof: polynomial case followed by general case

proof.text:
Apply [lem-pur-fp-algebra-module-generic-freeness] with $A=P$ (no algebra relations) and the finitely presented module $L$. Obtain $0
e a\in R$ with $L_a$ free over $R_a$. The map $L_a	o M_a$ is surjective by lifting numerators. If $\ell/a^j$ maps to zero, some $a^k\ell$ is in $\ker(L	o M)$; the preceding step supplies $0
e s\in R$ with $sa^k\ell=0$. Thus $s(\ell/a^j)=0$ in $L_a$. Since $R_a$ embeds in $K$ by $r/a^j\mapsto r/a^j$, $s/1
e0$; multiplication by $s/1$ is injective on each coordinate of the free module $L_a$. Therefore $\ell/a^j=0$, and $L_a	o M_a$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 051T, algebra-lemma-generic-flatness, proof: polynomial case followed by general case

proof.text: The finite presentation $P^u\to P^t\to L\to0$ with columns $n_i$ localizes to $P_a^u\to P_a^t\to L_a\to0$. Indeed a vector $v/a^j$ mapping to zero has $a^kv\in H$ for some $k$, so writing $a^kv=\sum_i c_i n_i$ expresses that vector as $\sum_i(c_i/a^{j+k})(n_i/1)$; every fraction in $L_a$ lifts a numerator in $P^t$. Use the isomorphism of the preceding step to replace $L_a$ by $M_a$. Thus the kernel of $P_a^t\to M_a$ is generated by these finitely many localized columns.

source.place: Tag 051T, algebra-lemma-generic-flatness, proof: polynomial case followed by general case

proof.text: The map $P_a\to B_a$ is surjective by lifting numerators. Map the finitely many relation columns $n_i/1$ into $B_a^t$. They generate $\ker(B_a^t\to M_a)$: lift any vector of this kernel coefficientwise to $P_a^t$; its image in $M_a$ is still zero, so it is a linear combination of the relation columns by the preceding step; reduce that expression to $B_a$. The columns map to zero, giving the reverse inclusion. Consequently $B_a^u\to B_a^t\to M_a\to0$ is the required finite presentation. All arguments allow $t=0$, $u=0$, $B=0$, and a zero generic fibre.
